result.title: Contextual Decision Making: Predictive or Generative
result.summary: Contextual decision making uses observed covariates to guide decisions under uncertainty. Two natural approaches are predict-then-optimize (PtO), which learns the conditional expected objective, and generate-then-optimize (GtO), which learns conditional uncertainty and optimizes using generated scenarios. We study when each approach is preferable by examining how the choice of learning target affects statistical accuracy and optimization tractability. Although PtO learns a narrower target, our regret bounds show how differences in smoothness can offset GtO's additional dimensional burden. Exploiting smoothness also raises an optimization tradeoff: within the class of nonnegative-weight PtO methods studied, a lower bound limits the gains from additional smoothness, while more flexible methods may introduce signed weights and lose the guarantee of preserving convexity. GtO preserves scenario-wise convexity, but requires learning a richer object and generating scenarios for optimization. Synthetic experiments and a real case study illustrate how these tradeoffs vary with data availability and problem structure. Together with the scope for reusing a model across tasks, our findings provide practical guidance for choosing between the approaches without identifying a universal winner.

AI.brief_summary: 论文比较上下文决策中的两条路线：「先预测再优化」（学习条件期望目标）与「先生成再优化」（学习条件不确定性并采样场景后优化），用 regret 界和优化可行性分析二者在光滑性、维度负担与凸性保持上的取舍，并以合成实验与真实案例说明其随数据量和问题结构变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预测期望目标 vs 生成条件场景」的统计—优化权衡，或可类比 LVR 中直接预测答案的 latent 与建模分布/多样假设的 latent 之间的选择，光滑性与维度代价的分析可供核查是否会迁移到推理状态设计。
